# Studying the Global Economy

---

# Course Objectives

<br>

For this class we will


* study workhorse models explaining why countries/firms trade

--


* analyze theoretical and empirical applications of these models

--

* think critically about the current state of the literature

--

* develop original research ideas

# Research Topic I: Trade/Transport

<br>

Trade relies heavily on containerships (60-70% of global trade volume)

* Asymmetric demand across bilateral trade routes

* Net outflows of loaded containers (e.g. US-China)

* Empty container repositioning $\implies$ .hi-pink[endogenous transport costs]

* How does government intervention (e.g. OSRA 2022) influence trade outcomes?


Challenges: Data availability ($), complex theoretical models


---

CF: .hi-pink[Moderate restriction to US empty container outflows]

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%"}
include_graphics("img/res.png")
```

* Cost of servicing assymetric lanes has risen, inducing price response<small>

  * Import leg $\rightarrow$ freight rate increase
  
  * Export leg $\rightarrow$ freight rate decline</small>
  
--
  
* Imports $\downarrow$, exports $\uparrow$ $\implies$ overall trade falls


--

* Pronounced decline in trade with East Asian trade partners

# Research Topics II: Multinational Firms

Developments in transportation and communication...

$\implies$ fragmentation of production across national borders

$\implies$ growth in multinational corporations


Conventional main questions:

* Why do some firms own subsidiaries abroad?

* Which factors determine the location of foreign subsidiaries?

* How is production and employment best organized across locations?

---

# Research Topics II: Multinational Firms


Growing focus on MNEs placing assets in low-tax jurisdictions

“Measuring Economic Activity in the Presence of Superstar MNEs”<br>(w. G. Nikolaishvili) .hi-pink[Economics Letters, 2023. Volume 226, 111077]

* How do these large shifts in strategic locations of ownership of intellectual property influence domestic economies?

* Main finding $-$ MNE presence in Ireland has inflated GDP by 22% relative to what state of domestic economy suggests

* Secondary finding $-$ No relationship between shocks to profit-shifting activity of MNEs and domestic economy

# Research Topics III: Environment/Trade

Global shipping emissions undermine extent to which trade fuels welfare gains

How do new logistical/queuing systems influence emissions?

My work:

* Considers the new queue system at LA/LB which assigns queue positions based on vessels' estimated time of arrival

* Prior system assigned queue positions upon reaching within 20 nautical miles of LA/LB, incentivized speeding

* How did new system influence global and local emissions?


---

class: clear-slide

<br>


```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%"}
include_graphics("img/global_emm.png")
```



New system delivers per-vessel emission reductions of approximately 10 per cent

---
class: clear-slide

<br>


```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%"}

```

Driven by a reduction of time spent queuing/idling in local area.

---


class: clear-slide

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%"}

```


Local air quality monitors suggest that air quality .hi-pink[deteriorated]

* Within 25-mile radius vs outer 25-50 mile ring <small><br>(difference out shocks across LA)</small>

* Within 25-mile LA/LB vs Within 25-mile control ports <small><br>(difference out shocks across ports)</small>

Same magnitude of effect across both DiDs.

# Key Facts (I)

<br>

* Trade is important: it grows really fast

* Trade is related to economic growth

* Country size is related to global market integration (trade openness)


---

# International Trade

<br>

Main Questions:

* Why do countries trade? What are the main determinants of trade?

* What are the gains from trade?

* Does trade cause income growth?

<br>

**Part I of the course focuses on theories of international trade.**


---


# International Trade

<br>

<br>

Main Questions:

* What goods does each country trade?

* How does trade affect specialization?

<br>

Countries specialize and export core products/sectors

Trading the goods that countries are "best" at $\rightarrow$ gains from trade

Dynamics in top ranking of export products

Factors other than country fundamentals influence specialization?

<small>

* knowledge diffusion?

* foreign direct investments (FDI)?

* cross-border migration?

</small>

# Key Facts (III)

<br>


<br>

* Explicit trade barriers (e.g., transport costs and tariffs) have decreased over time

* Hidden barriers to trade still play an important role

**Identifying and measuring trade costs has important policy implications.**


---

# Firm Level Export Activity

<br>

So far... facts about country level or industry-level trade

Zooming-in:
- firm level decision to participate in international trade

**Main questions:**

* Who participates in global markets?

* What are the characteristics of exporting firms?

# Key Facts (IV)

<br>

* Exporting is rare: few firms export + small share of output exported

* Exporting firms are "better" than domestic firms<br><small>
(e.g., sales, productivity, employment, etc.)</small>

* Most exporters enter few foreign markets and sell few products

* Top exporters responsible for most of trade by value

**Firm heterogeneity plays an important role in trade models.**

---

## Theories of International Trade

---


# Theories

<br>

Two strands within the field of international trade:

1) **Neoclassical models of trade** ('old' theories):

$\rightarrow$ Ricardian model

$\rightarrow$ Heckscher-Ohlin model

2) **'New' trade theory**:

$\rightarrow$ Krugman model

$\rightarrow$ Melitz model
